subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Should this issue stay open until maintainers have current-main Windows/provider proof for the fresh-session billing path, or are the shipped/current source guardrails enough to close it?
rationale: The report has serious real billing evidence, while current source shows multiple guardrails but no exact live proof that the observed provider input tokens are gone.

options.title: Require Live Current-Main Proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer or trusted proof run shows the reported fresh-session flow with large trajectory sidecars no longer inflates provider input tokens.

options.title: Close As Sufficiently Guarded
options.body: Close based on the artifact and memory filters already present, accepting the residual risk that a different runtime path caused the billing evidence.

options.title: Add A Defensive Guardrail
options.body: Sponsor a narrow follow-up that asserts trajectory sidecars cannot be selected by CLI/TUI startup, reseed, memory sync, or session history readers before closing.

recommendation.title: Require Live Current-Main Proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer or trusted proof run shows the reported fresh-session flow with large trajectory sidecars no longer inflates provider input tokens.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent token-pressure work and maintainer proof comments make this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
